newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firmer as market remains tight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firmer as market remains tight.

text.p: Interbank rates were firmer on Thursday as commercial banks and finance companies sought fresh funds in the tight market, dealers said.
"Rates are firming again as the market remains tight," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "Even commercial banks are bidding this morning."
One- and two-week money were at 8.70/80 percent against 8.50/70 percent on Wednesday.
One-month money was at 8.60/70 percent from 8.50 percent, and three-month was at 8.45/50 percent against 8.30 percent.
Dealers said a big local bank, which is also an agent bank of Bank Negara Malaysia, was seen lending one-month money at 8.60 percent.
"But the amount was small and had no impact on rates," another dealer said.
Dealers said they were unsure whether the bank was lending on behalf of the central bank, which has been injecting fresh funds into the market for the past two weeks to provide much-needed liquidity.
They said despite the central bank lending, the market was too short to prevent a spike-up in rates.
But rates could come off slightly on Friday due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit, dealers said.
The overnight rate was expected to continue trading around 8.50 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board to reflect firmer interbank rates.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down eight points to 92.15, or an implied yield of 7.85 percent.
The December contract was down three to 92.45, or 7.55 percent.
